# pbs_apt_repository (Resource)

Enables or disables an existing entry of the APT source files of a Proxmox Backup Server node, such as the enterprise repository on a host without a subscription. The counterpart of `proxmox_apt_repository` in bpg/proxmox.

The entry is addressed by its file and its index in the file, as PBS lists them; `pbs_apt_repositories` lists them all, and `pbs_apt_standard_repository` and `pbs_apt_repositories` tell where the entry of a standard repository is. PBS adds entries only for standard repositories, with `pbs_apt_standard_repository`, and removes none, so this resource neither adds nor removes one: creating it takes over an entry that is there, and destroying it leaves the entry as it is, enabled or not.

An index counts the entries before it in the same file. Should someone add or remove one of them outside Terraform, the index points to another entry. The provider tells them apart by their package types, URIs, suites and components: a refresh then warns and keeps the entry the state records, an update fails rather than change the other entry, and the warning says where the recorded entry is now, if it is still in the file. Editing an entry's URIs, suites or components outside Terraform looks the same; replace the resource to take over the entry as it is.

PBS rewrites the whole file when it enables or disables an entry: it normalises the formatting, and comment lines move to the top of their entry.

Reading the source files needs `Sys.Audit on /`, changing them `Sys.Modify on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A host without a subscription: the enterprise repository, which PBS
# installs enabled, is turned off, and the no-subscription repository is
# added in its place.
resource "pbs_apt_repository" "enterprise" {
  file_path = "/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources"
  index     = 0
  enabled   = false
}

resource "pbs_apt_standard_repository" "no_subscription" {
  handle = "no-subscription"
}

# Rather than written down, the place of a standard repository's entry can
# be looked up, here for the test repository, should the host have one.
data "pbs_apt_repositories" "this" {}

locals {
  test = one([
    for r in data.pbs_apt_repositories.this.standard_repositories : r
    if r.handle == "test" && r.file_path != null
  ])
}

resource "pbs_apt_repository" "test" {
  count = local.test == null ? 0 : 1

  file_path = local.test.file_path
  index     = local.test.index
  enabled   = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether APT uses the entry. PBS disables an entry of a `.list` file by commenting it out and one of a `.sources` file with `Enabled: false`.
- `file_path` (String) Path of the APT source file that holds the entry: `/etc/apt/sources.list`, or a `.list` or `.sources` file in `/etc/apt/sources.list.d`, such as `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `index` (Number) Position of the entry in the file, from 0. Disabled entries count — in a `.list` file, a commented-out line —, and a stanza of a `.sources` file is one entry, however many URIs or suites it lists. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node whose APT source files to manage: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. PBS is a single node, so both name the same files: do not manage one entry or repository under both. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `comment` (String) Comment lines above the entry, without their `#`, one per line; null when there are none.
- `components` (List of String) Components of the entry, such as `pbs-no-subscription`; empty for an absolute suite.
- `file_type` (String) Format of the file: `list` for one-line entries, `sources` for deb822 stanzas.
- `id` (String) `<node>,<file_path>,<index>`, such as `localhost,/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources,0`.
- `package_types` (List of String) Package types of the entry: `deb`, `deb-src`.
- `suites` (List of String) Suites of the entry, such as `trixie`.
- `uris` (List of String) URIs of the entry, such as `http://download.proxmox.com/debian/pbs`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_apt_repository.enterprise
  identity = {
    node      = "localhost"
    file_path = "/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources"
    index     = 0
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `file_path` (String) Path of the APT source file.
- `index` (Number) Index of the entry in the file, from 0.
- `node` (String) Node name, such as `localhost`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_apt_repository.enterprise
  id = "localhost,/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources,0"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An entry is imported by <node>,<file path>,<index>, as in bpg/proxmox: the
# node is localhost or the node's host name, and the index counts the
# entries of the file from 0, disabled ones included.
terraform import pbs_apt_repository.enterprise localhost,/etc/apt/sources.list.d/pbs-enterprise.sources,0
```
